clue.text: A plucky native warrior

explanation.surface: A courageous fighter from an indigenous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky is a synonym for courageous; a brave is a historical term for a Native American fighter.

clue.text: I vary a design for a cage

indicators.note: to design something is to plan and arrange it, so these letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks the plans for a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges IVARYA, the letters of 'I vary a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure where birds are kept, a kind of cage.

clue.text: Transferred and given a job

explanation.surface: An employee moved and handed a new role.
explanation.definitionFit: Property rights can be assigned (transferred) to another; a worker assigned a task has been allocated it.

clue.text: In any case, it has to be a silly remark

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so the first phrase surrounds the word it

parts.note: taken as written, run together
taken as written

explanation.surface: Whatever the circumstances, a foolish comment it must be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' looks like a stock phrase; 'case' is the container, putting IT inside INANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An inanity is a pointless, empty statement, so a foolish thing said.

clue.text: A porter I make use of in African city

indicators.note: making use of something can mean working it into a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone employs a hotel porter in a South African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make use of' rearranges APORTERI, the letters of 'A porter I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital, a city on that continent.

clue.text: Includes firm politician who gets to his feet

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
to stand up is to rise

explanation.surface: A list includes a company and a member of parliament who stands to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a Member of Parliament, the British elected representative.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to consist of or contain, a synonym for including.

clue.text: Cemetery to close in Kent

parts.note: a cemetery is a place full of graves
to close something is to end it

explanation.surface: A graveyard is shut down somewhere in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place itself: Kent is an English county, and Gravesend is a town on the Thames there. 'in Kent' stands for a town found in that county.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a riverside town located within the county of Kent, so a place in that county.

clue.text: To make a mistake or to make a mistake

parts.note: to err is to go wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deliberately repetitive phrase, as if the writer stammered.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition is a joke: the first 'To make a mistake' gives ERR, the 'or' is itself, and the second gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a blunder or slip, the noun sense of a wrong move.

clue.text: Take off the orange cover

explanation.surface: Remove the outer layer of a piece of citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel is to strip away; the peel is the rind on fruit such as an orange.

clue.text: Flying over a Roman road, not one well-aligned

annotationWithheld.why: 'Flying over a Roman road, not one well-aligned' (8) AVIATION: A + VIA gives AVIA, but no reading of 'not one well-aligned' yields TION; the clue appears garbled as held and a search of its text found nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Flying over a Roman road, not one well-aligned

clue.text: Legally blocks return of containers in el Salvador

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, the containers sitting within the country code

parts.note: ES is the international code for El Salvador

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the word for containers is read backwards

parts.note: pots are containers

explanation.surface: A Central American country's courts stop goods coming back in shipping containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns POTS into STOP, which goes inside ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term for barring someone from asserting a claim, so it prevents by law.

clue.text: A song written for the man by ear

indicators.note: something judged by ear is judged as heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: him refers to a man

explanation.surface: A tune composed for a particular fellow, played without sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by ear' signals that HIM sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise.

clue.text: In a trice, leg broken, as if by telepathy

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: In an instant someone's leg snaps, as though by mind power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges TRICELEG, the letters of 'trice, leg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Telergic describes action at a distance by the mind alone, the mechanism imagined behind thought transfer.

clue.text: Spot a number wanting to snoop

parts.note: e is the mathematical constant, a number
to snoop is to spy

explanation.surface: A digit eager to pry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' is e, the mathematical constant about 2.718.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a synonym for noticing.

clue.text: Two-thirds of message to church in Devon

indicators.note: two of a three-letter word's letters are kept, one being dropped

parts.note: a fax is a message sent by telephone line
a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: Part of a note sent to a church in a county of south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' drops F from FAX, leaving AX. Devon is a county in south-west England; Axminster is a town there, famous for carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a market town located within Devon, so a place in that county.

clue.text: Terrapin found in quite mysterious circumstances

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters these words make

explanation.surface: A turtle is discovered under puzzling conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' picks the run between quitE and MYSterious.
explanation.definitionFit: Emys is the genus name of a group of freshwater turtles, the pond terrapins.

clue.text: A poor average

explanation.surface: A mediocre arithmetic result.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can mean shabby or inferior; it is also the arithmetic average of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Force out former spouse? True, but keeping daughter

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the word true holds the next letter

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone ejects an ex-partner, though admits a child stays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts D inside TRUE, giving TRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to push or squeeze material out through an opening.

clue.text: Puts up once more with raise in research

indicators.note: one word sits inside another, the raising word within research

parts.note: RES is an abbreviation for research
to erect is to raise

explanation.surface: A team builds again after a funding increase for research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ERECT inside RES.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-erect is to set upright or build again, a second construction.

clue.text: Grand homes one's friend got first

indicators.note: the friend comes first, before the next piece

parts.note: a pal is a friend
an ace is a one on dice or cards, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A mate gets to the big houses ahead of somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' read as 'ace's' gives ACES; 'got first' puts PAL in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaces are magnificent residences of royalty or the very rich.

clue.text: Place everyone would love a pet with energy to have

parts.note: all means everyone
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a cat is a pet
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Everybody would adore a lively pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is O because a nil score in tennis is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to assign or put in position, a sense of placing.

clue.text: Alcohol radical uses in the morning, year long

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is before noon

explanation.surface: A drinker takes a stiff dose early every day all year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amyl is the chemical group C5H11, found in pentanols, a component of certain alcohols.

clue.text: 17 the German takes for a ramble

parts.note: the answer to 17 down is used here
der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A stingy German heads off on a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' refers to the answer at 17 down, MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly; a meander is a winding stroll.

clue.text: An extra earner for the team leading to a row

parts.note: a side is a team
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A second job for the squad leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is a secondary job or business done for income besides the main one.

clue.text: First person at a meeting of airlines association

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: The earliest arrival at an airline industry gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' is the grammatical first person, not the first to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: IATA is the International Air Transport Association, the trade body of airlines.

clue.text: Boys who are leading lights at drama society

indicators.note: leading letters are the ones at the front of each word

explanation.surface: Young men who are the stars of an amateur theatre group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' takes the first letters of lights, at, drama and society.
explanation.definitionFit: Lads is an informal word for youths or young fellows.

clue.text: Point to mature years as cause of senility

parts.note: a dot is a point
age is what brings on senility

explanation.surface: Indicating that growing old leads to mental decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mature years' is the definition, leaving 'as cause of senility' to give AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of old age, often with weakened faculties.

clue.text: Unbeliever finds god in Georgia

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, the state abbreviation going into the god

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: An atheist discovers a deity in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: GA goes inside PAN, splitting it after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, one outside the main world religions.

clue.text: Mixed-up cats joining in exercises? That's one way of looking at it!

definitions.text: one way of looking at it

indicators.note: the exercises piece goes into the middle of the jumbled cats
mixed-up letters are jumbled, so the word cats is rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Confused felines taking part in a workout, viewed as a quirky angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed-up' gives ASCT from CATS, and 'joining in' puts PE inside after AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a particular view or facet of a matter.

clue.text: Deplorable inaction concerning tobacco

indicators.note: something deplorable is in a bad state, so the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: Shameful failure to act on smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deplorable' rearranges INACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotian relates to the tobacco plant, genus Nicotiana, named after Jean Nicot.

clue.text: Note the peculiar dentition

parts.note: te is a note in tonic sol-fa

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the word the is jumbled

explanation.surface: Remarking on someone's odd set of teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentition is the arrangement of a set of chompers in the mouth, the collective for them.

clue.text: Star held in, having gained a little weight

parts.note: pent means confined, as in pent-up
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A celebrity, kept indoors, has put on a bit of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity but is the five-pointed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star shape.
